title: fcs: $PnR bit mask never applied to integer parameter data
description:
Reported upstream: https://github.com/jrmoynihan/flow/issues/21 (item 1)

parse_uniform_data_bulk() and parse_parameter_value_to_f32() in fcs/src/file.rs (~L614-L800) read raw u16/u32 integers via byteorder and cast straight to f32 with zero masking against $PnR. $PnR is parsed/stored but the only consumer is compress.rs:317 (codec width selection for compression).

FCS 3.1/3.2 both mandate masking: field width ($PnB) is often wider than the parameter's true resolution ($PnR), e.g. 10-bit ADC data stored in a 16-bit field with 6 garbage/unused high bits. Common on Beckman FC500/Gallios/Navios and analog-era BD instruments. Currently these files parse without error but produce silently wrong channel values.
acceptance_criteria: mask = next_power_of_two($PnR) - 1 computed per-parameter and applied via (value & mask) before the f32 cast, in both the bulk rayon path and the scalar/cold path in file.rs. Regression test with a synthetic 10-bit-in-16-bit fixture FCS file confirms masked values match expected range.
close_reason: Fixed: added Metadata::get_range_for_channel(); file.rs column-extraction loop now masks integer parameters to ($PnR.next_power_of_two() - 1) before building the DataFrame column. Test added in fcs/src/write.rs (pnr_mask_strips_garbage_high_bits_from_int16_data) confirmed red against pre-fix code, green after. Full fcs suite (76 tests) + clippy clean.

title: tru-ols: unmixed export writes empty $PnS into FCS3.2 files, corrupting TEXT on reopen
description:
tru-ols/src/fcs_integration.rs inserts $PnS with an empty value at two sites — line 298 (unmixed parameters) and line 460 (autofluorescence, comment reads 'Leave $PnS blank for autofluorescence') — and line 520 then stamps the output FCS 3.2 via stamp_v3_2.

FCS 3.1+ forbids empty keyword values, precisely because a doubled delimiter is the escape for a literal delimiter in those versions. An empty value serialises to two adjacent delimiter bytes, which a conforming 3.1+ reader must decode as ONE escaped literal, not two field boundaries. The key therefore absorbs the following key and every later field shifts by one.

Surfaced by flow-crates-1xb Task 3, which version-gated un-doubling on read: the exported file no longer round-trips, and the panic dump shows the merged keyword $P4S$PLATENAME. Confirmed pre-existing via git stash — the corruption was always being written, it was simply symmetrically misread by our own version-blind tokenizer. Third-party 3.1+ readers would already have mis-parsed these files.

Test that catches it: flow-tru-ols fcs_integration::tests::test_unmixed_export_roundtrip_readable_without_acquisition_detectors.

Blocking relationship: flow-crates-1xb Task 4 makes an empty value under V3_1+ a hard write-time error, so write_fcs_file will start returning Err from these sites. This must be resolved before Task 4 can land green.

Two candidate fixes, and the choice is user-visible: (a) omit the $PnS insert entirely, which is the encoding FCS intends for 'no short name' — a downstream reader goes from Some("") to None; or (b) write a meaningful non-empty value such as the channel name or 'Autofluorescence'. Do NOT keep an empty value and weaken the reader.
acceptance_criteria: No tru-ols export path emits an empty keyword value in a file stamped FCS3.1 or later, and test_unmixed_export_roundtrip_readable_without_acquisition_detectors passes with the version-gated reader.
close_reason: Fixed in Task 3 of the flow-crates-3si/1xb plan. All three empty-$PnS write sites in tru-ols/src/fcs_integration.rs now emit a descriptive value instead of a blank: unmixed parameters (~line 307), the mixed/target path (~line 421), and autofluorescence (~line 493), each with a comment recording that FCS 3.1+ forbids empty keyword values and that a $PnS equal to $PnN is treated as 'no override' downstream. rg -n 'PnS' tru-ols/src/fcs_integration.rs shows no remaining blank insert. fcs_integration::tests::test_unmixed_export_roundtrip_readable_without_acquisition_detectors passes, as does the whole workspace (618/618 under nextest --profile ci).

title: fcs: derived Fcs values (filter/unmix/compensate) share a stale-prone column cache with their source
description:
Final whole-branch review of flow-crates-dzw's Stage A found a real hazard, latent in Stage A (no production callers of column()/columns() yet) but live once Stage B ships: several places clone an Fcs and mutate the clone's data_frame while leaving the Arc<[OnceLock<Box<[f32]>>]> columns cache shared with the source, because Fcs derives Clone and the cache field is Arc-shared by design (correct for the eventual Stage B world where Fcs never mutates, wrong for Stage A/interim code where these assignment sites still exist):

- fcs/src/write.rs:231-240 (filter_events): clones fcs, replaces data_frame with a filtered/shorter frame, updates $TOT to the new (smaller) count. Calling column() on the result builds a ColumnLayout sized to the NEW (smaller) num_events, decodes a raw PREFIX of the ORIGINAL unfiltered mmap bytes (extract_columns only errors when data is too short, not when it's simply a subset), and writes that wrong, silently-truncated value into the SHARED cache slot — poisoning the source Fcs too if it's still alive (e.g. sitting in an Arc<Fcs> cache).
- peacoqc-rs/src/lib.rs:332-337 (FcsFilter::filter): same clone-and-replace pattern; $TOT is explicitly NOT updated here, so column() returns a correct-length raw column that silently disagrees with data_frame.height() instead.
- tru-ols/src/fcs_integration.rs:200-230 (spectral unmixing output): clones stained_fcs, clears+replaces the parameter map, doesn't touch the columns cache size — see also flow-crates-3si's sibling finding about unchecked indexing panicking here if the new parameter count differs from the cache's original size.

Minimum documentation fix already applied in flow-crates-dzw's merge: a # Warning section on column()/columns()/events() stating they decode from the mmap and are only meaningful on an Fcs obtained from open()/open_all() — a clone whose data_frame was replaced still shares this cache and decodes against the ORIGINAL file bytes.

Real fix (deferred to Stage B, or before Stage B's own migration if column()/columns() gain production callers before then): decide how derived Fcs values get a FRESH, correctly-sized, empty cache instead of inheriting the shared Arc. Note this likely dissolves naturally once Stage B removes the mutation sites entirely (EventDataFrame becomes an owned, non-Fcs-mutating return value) — but if that lands after column()/columns() get real callers, this needs its own fix first. State this explicitly in the Stage B plan so it isn't rediscovered from scratch.

title: fcs: extract_columns allocates per-event, has no uniform-width fast path, calls #[cold] hot
description:
Final whole-branch review of flow-crates-dzw's Stage A (lazy per-column FCS loading) found that fcs/src/columns.rs's extract_columns materializes a Vec<Vec<f32>> (one allocation per event) before transposing into columns, and dispatches every value through Fcs::parse_parameter_value_to_f32 — a function annotated #[cold] specifically because it was previously only a rare fallback path in store_raw_data_as_dataframe. Calling a #[cold] function once per value in what is now a primary decode loop is a per-value pessimization by construction.

This is what actually produced Task 8's benchmark result (events_uncached ~8x slower than a bare Fcs::open(), which includes its own full eager parse) — not the 'two separate traversals' explanation recorded during implementation (iter_batched excludes setup-closure time, so open()'s cost isn't counted in that measurement at all).

For a 3M-event, 40-parameter file this transient Vec<Vec<f32>> intermediate is larger than the final column output for small requests, which undercuts the entire memory argument Stage B is being built to deliver. Fix: write directly into pre-sized per-column buffers (no Vec<Vec<f32>> intermediate, no per-event allocation), and add a uniform-width fast path comparable to the eager path's parse_uniform_data_bulk / bytemuck zero-copy branch for uniform F32. Either drop #[cold] from parse_parameter_value_to_f32 or introduce a non-cold variant for this hot loop. Add a test that actually exercises the par_chunks_exact (parallel) branch — currently zero test coverage exists for it (all existing tests use event counts well under PARALLEL_THRESHOLD).

This should be resolved, or at minimum re-benchmarked and the numbers understood, before Stage B is planned — Stage B's entire justification rests on the per-column extraction being cheap.
notes:
AFTER (post-rewrite), criterion paired A/B: 2c8f09f --save-baseline pre vs HEAD --baseline pre, shared CRITERION_HOME, bench file byte-identical at both commits. Apple M5 Max, 18 cores.
  two_column_access/lazy_columns_uncached  = 28.67 us (was 251.9 us, 8.8x; criterion -88.24%, p=0.00)
  full_materialization/events_uncached     = 77.64 us (was 640.5 us, 8.3x; criterion -87.87%, p=0.00)
  synthetic_1Mx20/one_column_of_twenty     = 1.121 ms (was 11.06 ms, 9.9x; criterion -89.81%, p=0.00)
  synthetic_1Mx20/all_twenty_columns       = 5.449 ms (was 110.7 ms, 20.3x; criterion -95.17%, p=0.00)
Untouched controls open_eager_baseline and eager_data_frame_two_columns both moved ~+2% over the same paired runs, which is this machine's drift floor. events_uncached (77.6us) is now cheaper than open_eager_baseline (83.8us); the original 8x gap is gone, not merely reduced.

PARALLEL_BYTE_THRESHOLD LEFT AT 1 MiB, and 256 KiB is now positively ruled out by measurement.
Stage 1, the sweep over the committed bench fixtures, was uninformative and could not have been otherwise: int-10000_events_random.fcs has a 234 KiB DATA segment and stays sequential at all three candidates, and the synthetic fixture has a 76.3 MiB DATA segment and goes parallel at all three, so all three configurations execute identical machine code and the spread between them is noise by construction.
Stage 2 probed the crossover on the one corpus file that does land in the window: fcs2_int16_50000ev_8par_random.fcs, $TOT 50000 x $PAR 8 x $PnB 16 = 800,000 B = 781.25 KiB of DATA (confirmed by its header, $BEGINDATA 640 / $ENDDATA 800639) -- parallel at 256 KiB, sequential at 1 MiB and 4 MiB. Pointing compliance_fcs() at it as scaffolding (reverted; not committed) and running criterion interleaved under an isolated CRITERION_HOME, two cycles of 1 MiB --save-baseline then 256 KiB --baseline:
  cycle 1: sequential 162.54 us -> parallel 202.42 us, criterion +31.49% [+23.30, +40.84], p=0.00, 'Performance has regressed'
  cycle 2: sequential 139.58 us -> parallel 220.95 us, criterion +43.78% [+37.21, +50.72], p=0.00, 'Performance has regressed'
The untouched eager_data_frame_two_columns control moved +4.4% over cycle 2, so the effect is an order of magnitude outside the noise. At ~800 KB rayon's fan-out costs more than the decode it splits. Lowering the constant to 256 KiB would have made files of this size roughly 35% slower.
The 1 MiB - 4 MiB region is still unprobed -- no corpus fixture lands in it -- so a re-tune wanting to raise the constant would have to generate one. Tracked separately.

parse_parameter_value_to_f32 left untouched: its only remaining caller is parse_variable_width_data (file.rs:1547), which is itself #[cold], so the annotation is accurate by subtraction.
Uniform-decoder monomorphization still deferred -- the numbers do NOT justify revisiting it. one_column_of_twenty moves 76.3 MiB in 1.12 ms (~71 GB/s aggregate), i.e. memory-bandwidth bound, not dispatch bound; eliminating a perfectly-predicted enum branch cannot buy anything there.
close_reason: extract_columns rewritten: per-column Decoder resolved once (fcs/src/decode.rs), infallible inner loop, pre-sized alloc_zeroed output buffers, no Vec<Vec<f32>> intermediate, parallel branch via split_at_mut driven by PARALLEL_BYTE_THRESHOLD (bytes walked, not values kept). Parallel branch now has coverage; oracle widened from 1 column of 1 file to every parameter of every corpus file. Before/after in this issue's notes.

title: fcs: $NEXTDATA treated as file-absolute, but §3.3.31 defines it data-set-relative
description:
FCS 3.2 §3.3.31: "The value of the $NEXTDATA keyword specifies the byte offset from the beginning of A DATA SET to the first byte in the HEADER of the next data set in the FCS file."

Two discrepancies with Fcs::open_all (fcs/src/file.rs:498):

1. RELATIVE VS ABSOLUTE. The loop feeds next_data_offset straight into header_for_dataset_at(&mmap, next_data_offset, ...) (file.rs:536) as a file-absolute position, and the doc comment at file.rs:483 states that reading explicitly. Correct per spec is dataset_start + next_data_offset. These coincide for dataset 2 only, because dataset 1 begins at byte 0. A 3+ dataset chain lands at the wrong offset and either errors out of find_begindata_offset or, worse, mis-parses whatever bytes happen to be there. Fix: carry a running dataset_start through the loop.

2. HEADER VS TEXT. The spec says $NEXTDATA points at the next data set HEADER; header_for_dataset_at treats the target as the first byte of that data set TEXT segment (reads mmap[text_start] as the delimiter) and synthesises a Header instead of parsing a real 58-byte one. This may well be deliberate vendor tolerance -- the traversal was added against real .lmd exports in 6986541 -- so investigate before changing. If real files do carry a per-dataset HEADER, prefer parsing it and falling back to the synthetic path.

3. Related, to confirm while in here: header_for_dataset_at builds text_offset as text_start..=(begin_data - 1), mixing an absolute text_start with a $BEGINDATA value that §2.2.4 arguably makes data-set-relative as well.

Found while implementing flow-crates-x17.3; is_first_dataset()/computed_crc() sidestep it by refusing to compute a CRC for any dataset past the first.
acceptance_criteria: A synthetic 3-dataset chain round-trips through open_all with all three datasets parsed correctly, and a test asserts the second hop resolves to dataset2_start + $NEXTDATA rather than the bare offset. The file.rs:483 doc comment states the spec definition. Whether dataset 2+ carries a real HEADER is answered in the issue notes with evidence from a real multi-dataset file.
notes:
RESOLVED. Scope was wider than the bead assumed: nothing in the crate modelled a data set origin at all, so this was not a $NEXTDATA arithmetic slip but a missing coordinate system.

Implementation:
- Fcs gains 'pub dataset_start: usize' (byte offset of the data set's first byte; 0 for the first). Made pub, not pub(crate), so external struct literals stay fixable - the mistake recorded in flow-crates-3nt.
- Header now keeps its offsets exactly as written = data-set-RELATIVE. New Header::from_bytes(&[u8]); from_mmap is the base==0 wrapper. The get_* helpers widened from &Mmap to &[u8] (source-compatible via deref coercion). HEADER_SIZE moved to header.rs; write.rs re-exports it.
- New private fn absolutize(offset, dataset_start, file_len, what) is the single place the two coordinate systems meet. It does NOT assume the spec reading: offset < dataset_start can only be relative; otherwise prefer relative unless it runs past EOF, in which case read as file-absolute and tracing::warn. This is what keeps the pre-existing absolute-style two-dataset test green as a vendor-tolerance regression.
- resolve_segment_offsets(header, metadata, dataset_start, file_len) now returns FILE-ABSOLUTE ranges. TEXT split out into text_range() because metadata cannot be read until TEXT is located, so it must resolve without metadata.
- Metadata::from_text_segment(mmap, &RangeInclusive) added; from_mmap delegates.
- Q2 ANSWERED: yes, §2.4.2 makes a per-data-set HEADER mandatory. header_for_dataset_at now tries a real 58-byte Header::from_bytes first and only falls back to the $BEGINDATA scan for vendors that omit it. Q3 confirmed: the synthetic header collapses from the buggy text_start..=(begin_data-1) to a correct relative 0..=(begin_data-dataset_start-1).
- open_all's loop guard keys on dataset_start, not TEXT offset - under the relative model every data set reports the same TEXT offset (58, or 0 headerless), which would have looked like a loop on the first hop.
- is_first_dataset() is now 'dataset_start == 0' (const fn), replacing the re-parse hack.

Test: write.rs open_all_resolves_nextdata_relative_to_each_dataset_start builds a fully spec-conformant 3-data-set file (per-data-set HEADER, all offsets relative) and asserts all[2].dataset_start == all[1].dataset_start + $NEXTDATA. Verified to FAIL under the old absolute reading (chain-loop error) and pass after - the two-data-set test passes either way, which is exactly why this was latent.

Cost: 'dataset_start' had to be added to 11 Fcs struct literals across fcs, tru-ols, gates, peacoqc-rs (all 0).
close_reason: Implemented: FCS offsets are now data-set-relative throughout, with vendor-tolerant absolute fallback. 147 flow-fcs tests + 47 workspace test binaries green; no new clippy warnings (52 before and after).

title: fcs: pub(crate) Fcs.columns field breaks struct-literal Fcs construction across peacoqc-rs, gates, tru-ols, and flow-fcs's own compress-feature tests
description:
Commit 254049e (feat(fcs): add Fcs::column and Fcs::columns lazy cached accessors,
part of the lazy-fcs-column-loading Stage A work) added a new field to the public
`Fcs` struct:

    pub(crate) columns: std::sync::Arc<[std::sync::OnceLock<Box<[f32]>>]>,

`Fcs`'s other fields (header, metadata, parameters, data_frame, file_access) are
all `pub`, so external crates have historically constructed `Fcs` directly via
struct-literal syntax in their own test fixtures. Because the new field is only
`pub(crate)`, any such external struct literal now fails to compile with
"cannot construct `flow_fcs::Fcs` with struct literal syntax due to private
fields ... missing field `columns`".

Two call sites are currently broken:

1. `tru-ols/src/fcs_integration.rs:852,1205,1355` (inside `#[cfg(test)] mod
   tests`) — `flow-tru-ols`'s own test suite fails to compile, independent of
   any workspace feature unification:

       cargo test -p flow-tru-ols --lib
       error: cannot construct `flow_fcs::Fcs` with struct literal syntax due
       to private fields ... missing field `columns`  (x3)

2. `fcs/src/compress.rs:382` (`build_test_fcs`, `#[cfg(test)]`, gated behind
   flow-fcs's own `compress` feature, which is off by default) — this one is
   *inside* flow-fcs, so `columns` is technically visible, but the helper was
   never updated to supply it:

       cargo test -p flow-fcs --features compress
       error[E0063]: missing field `columns` in initializer of `file::Fcs`

Neither call site was touched by any commit in the lazy-fcs-column-loading
Stage A branch (edfea89..HEAD), confirming this is a gap in Task 4's rollout
rather than a regression introduced later. It was not caught earlier because
Task 4/5's own verification only ran `cargo test -p flow-fcs` with default
features, which exercises neither the `compress` feature nor the `tru-ols`
crate. It surfaced during Task 6's `cargo test --workspace` verification pass.

Minimal fixes for the two known sites:
- `fcs/src/compress.rs`: same-crate, pub(crate) is visible — just add
  `columns: std::iter::repeat_with(std::sync::OnceLock::new).take(3).collect(),`
  to the `Fcs { ... }` literal in `build_test_fcs`, mirroring the fix already
  applied to `fcs/src/tests.rs` in commit 254049e.
- `tru-ols/src/fcs_integration.rs`: cross-crate, `pub(crate)` cannot be named
  externally at all — needs an actual API decision, e.g. a `#[cfg(any(test,
  feature = "test-util"))]` public constructor/builder on `Fcs` for
  fixture-building, or loosening `columns` visibility, or a `Default`-based
  functional-update path. Whoever owns the `Fcs` public API for Stage A
  should choose the approach; this bead documents the break rather than
  prescribing the fix.

Verified via:
  cargo test --workspace          # fails to compile flow-tru-ols and flow-fcs
  cargo test -p flow-tru-ols --lib  # fails independent of workspace features
close_reason: Already fixed on main: Fcs::for_testing(header, metadata, parameters, data_frame, file_access) added at fcs/src/file.rs:425 under #[cfg(any(test, feature="test-util"))], sizing the columns cache to parameters.len(); new fcs 'test-util' feature (fcs/Cargo.toml:130) consumed by tru-ols dev-dep. All struct-literal sites migrated (tru-ols/src/fcs_integration.rs:911,1264,1414, tru-ols/src/provenance.rs:472, fcs/src/compress.rs:387, fcs/src/tests.rs:55, fcs/src/write.rs:1067,1291,2140). Verified: 'cargo test -p flow-tru-ols --lib --no-run' and 'cargo test -p flow-fcs --features compress --no-run' both Finished.

title: fcs: writer does not escape the TEXT delimiter inside keyword values
description:
serialize_metadata (fcs/src/write.rs:570) joins keys and values with metadata.delimiter but never doubles an occurrence of that byte inside a value. FCS 3.1/3.2 requires the delimiter to be escaped by repetition when it appears in a value.

Consequence: any value containing the delimiter silently truncates and desynchronizes the whole remainder of TEXT on reopen. Reproduced with a space-delimited file and $LAST_MODIFIER = 'flow-tru-ols 0.1.0': every subsequent keyword including $P1N was lost, and Fcs::open failed with 'No $P1N keyword stored'.

Every writer test in the crate works around this by setting metadata.delimiter = '\u{000c}' first (write.rs:978, 1093, 1192, 1282, 1378, 1459, 1616), and build_unmixed_fcs_from_unmixed_abundances does the same at runtime. That workaround only moves the problem: free-text keywords ($UNSTAINEDINFO, $PROJ, $COM) can contain a form feed too, and $TRUOLS_MIXMAT cannot contain a comma-delimited value if the delimiter is a comma.

Fix: double the delimiter byte when writing each key and value, and un-double on read. Also reject NUL as a delimiter.
acceptance_criteria: A value containing the active delimiter round-trips through write -> Fcs::open unchanged, for a space delimiter, a comma delimiter and a form-feed delimiter; the read path un-doubles; existing files still parse.
notes: Post-close annotation, recorded for honesty rather than to reopen. This issue was closed at commit 167c7ff partly on the strength of a characterisation test that pinned tokenizer agreement across a $NEXTDATA chain with escaping. A later task established that that particular lock is unfalsifiable as written -- it cannot fail for the reason it claims to guard, because the two tokenizers it compares agree by construction on the input it builds. The SHIPPED BEHAVIOUR is unaffected and is independently covered: the version gate lives in fcs/src/text.rs Escaping::for_version, the write-side empty-value rejection is a hard error under V3_1+, and all 10 corpus files round-trip. Deliberately not reopened -- the fix is to strengthen or delete that one test, which is cheap and not worth reverting a closed issue for. See also flow-crates-2s7 (pre-3.1 raw delimiter corruption) and flow-crates-8px (retire the tru-ols SAFE_TEXT_DELIMITER workaround, now unblocked).
close_reason: Escaping implemented in fcs/src/text.rs, gated at Version::V3_1 (3.1 is the first version forbidding empty values, which is what makes doubling decodable -- the corpus's 5 consecutive-delimiter runs are all FCS2.0 empty values). title: fcs: serialize_metadata silently downgrades $BYTEORD to little-endian
description: write::serialize_metadata (fcs/src/write.rs:563) emits $BYTEORD by matching on Keyword::Byte(ByteKeyword::BYTEORD(_)) and falling back to the literal "1,2,3,4" for anything else. Metadata::insert_string_keyword bypasses match_and_parse_keyword, so a caller doing insert_string_keyword("\$BYTEORD", "4,3,2,1") stores StringKeyword::Other and the written file claims little-endian while the DATA segment was produced from big-endian source values. Silent, and it corrupts every numeric column. Found while writing the conformance \$BYTEORD rule (flow-crates-x17.4), which is why that rule judges the *value* via ByteOrder::from_keyword_str rather than the variant.
design: Two candidate fixes: (a) make insert_string_keyword route through match_and_parse_keyword so values land in their typed variant -- broader blast radius, likely the right long-term answer; (b) have serialize_metadata fall back to reading the raw string value via ByteOrder::from_keyword_str before defaulting. Whichever is chosen, the default must not be a silent literal: if no \$BYTEORD can be determined, the writer should error rather than guess an endianness.
acceptance_criteria: A round trip that inserts \$BYTEORD=4,3,2,1 as a plain string and writes the file produces a file whose \$BYTEORD reads back as 4,3,2,1; no code path emits a hardcoded byte order when metadata carries a different one.

title: fcs: write_inline_fcs baked a stale $BEGINDATA into TEXT
description:
Found and fixed while implementing flow-crates-x17.2.

write_inline_fcs (fcs/src/compress.rs) serialized the TEXT segment ONCE using the
estimated data offset, then computed the real offsets and corrected only the
HEADER. The $BEGINDATA/$ENDDATA baked into TEXT kept the estimated values and
disagreed with the HEADER - in the reproducer, TEXT said 808 while the HEADER
said 333.

Latent, not yet exploitable: every reader in this workspace prefers the HEADER
offsets, and file.rs store_raw_data_as_dataframe only consults $BEGINDATA when
the HEADER field is 0. So the stale value was never read.

It becomes silent data corruption the moment flow-crates-x17.1 lands. That fix
makes build_header write '       0' for offsets past 99,999,999 per the FCS
3.1/3.2 rule - which is precisely the condition that sends the reader to the
stale TEXT value. It would then decode the wrong byte range as events with no
error: wrong numbers, not a crash.

FIX: route write_inline_fcs through crate::write::resolve_layout so TEXT is
serialized with the offsets it actually declares.
acceptance_criteria:
Fixed. Regression test compress::tests::inline_fcs_text_begindata_agrees_with_header
parses the HEADER offset fields and the TEXT keywords from a written file and
asserts TEXT $BEGINDATA/$ENDDATA equal the HEADER values and that
header_data_start == text_end + 1.

Test verified to have teeth: temporarily restoring the one-shot logic makes it
fail with 'left: 808, right: 333'.

title: fcs: implement FCS 3.2 CRC read + write
description: No CRC support exists anywhere (rg -i crc fcs/src/ returns nothing). FCS 3.1 s3.5 (unchanged in 3.2) requires a 16-bit CCITT CRC, polynomial X^16+X^12+X^5, with each input character interpreted as its bit-reversed image (NR icrc(..., jinit=0, jrev=-1)), computed from the first HEADER byte through the last byte of the final segment, written as 8 ASCII bytes immediately after that segment; eight ASCII '0' means 'not computed'. We emit neither, so files are non-conformant even under the opt-out. New fcs/src/crc.rs with compute/format_field/parse_field and a StoredCrc enum. Write side covers BOTH writers: write_fcs_file (write.rs:127) and write_inline_fcs (compress.rs:183). Read side: Fcs::open warns on mismatch and continues (vendor files often carry absent/wrong CRCs); Fcs::open_verified returns Err. Locating the last segment must go through a shared resolve_segment_offsets(&Header, &Metadata) helper extracted from file.rs:546 -- Header::get_data_offsets returns raw HEADER bytes and reports 0..=0 for spec-conformant large files.
design: RISK: the reflection semantics decide between CRC-16/KERMIT and reflected-input XMODEM -- same polynomial, different check value. Do not guess. Transcribe the C++/C# reference implementations added in FCS 3.2 and validate against a real vendor file carrying a non-zero CRC. BLOCKED until the spec PDF is copied to docs/specs/ (macOS TCC blocks ~/Downloads; flowcyt.sourceforge.net is proxy-blocked).
acceptance_criteria: compute(b"123456789") matches the FCS 3.2 reference implementation with a comment naming the catalog variant; write/reopen round-trip verifies; a flipped DATA byte makes open_verified return Err and Fcs::open warn; CrcPolicy::Omit writes exactly b"00000000" as the final 8 bytes.
notes: UNBLOCKED 2026-08-06: spec at fcs/FCS v3.2 Specification.pdf (93pp). Normative text is s3.7 'CRC Value' (p.83), not s3.5. RESOLVED ALGORITHM - the spec supplies its own test vector, which uniquely determines the variant: 'the result of any compatible CRC calculation of the string CatMouse987654321 shall return 49805 (C28D hex)'. Brute-forcing poly 0x1021 over init/refin/refout/xorout yields exactly ONE match: init=0x0000, refin=true, refout=true, xorout=0x0000 == CRC-16/KERMIT, whose conventional check('123456789')=0x2189 (8585). Reflection risk is therefore closed WITHOUT the reference implementations (Appendix B is only sourceforge download URLs, still 403 behind Zscaler; the normative vector is stronger anyway since it pins behaviour not implementation). PLAN CORRECTION: the field is DECIMAL ASCII, not hex. Spec: 'a CRC value of 49805 (C28D hex) shall be encoded as 00049805', left-padded with 0 to 8 bytes => format!({crc:08}). The approved plan said hex '0000abcd' - that would have been silently unverifiable by conformant readers. Also confirmed: s3.8 white space (unused space outside HEADER/segments/CRC = ASCII 32); NEXTDATA offsets are data-set-relative (s3.3.31) so per-dataset CRC ranges are [ds_start, ds_start+last_segment_end], confirming x17.8 scope.
close_reason:
Implemented in fcs/src/crc.rs (new), with read/write wiring in file.rs, write.rs, compress.rs, lib.rs. 152 tests green (cargo test -p flow-fcs --lib --features compress); cargo check --workspace --all-targets clean; cargo test -p flow-tru-ols --features flow-fcs green.

ALGORITHM IDENTIFICATION. The bead design said "do not guess" the reflection semantics and named the Appendix B reference implementations as the way to settle it. Appendix B turned out to contain only sourceforge URLs, still 403 behind the proxy. Settled it a better way instead: §3.7 carries a NORMATIVE test vector -- compute("CatMouse987654321") == 49805 -- and brute-forcing the standard CRC-16 parameter space for poly 0x1021 against it yields exactly one match, CRC-16/KERMIT (init 0x0000, refin, refout, no xorout). Pinned by two tests, the FCS vector and the catalog check value 0x2189 for "123456789", so drift toward XMODEM (0x31C3) fails immediately. Behaviour-pinned and CI-checkable, which transcribed C++ would not have been.

PLAN CORRECTION. The approved plan specified a hex field ("0000abcd"). The spec mandates DECIMAL: "a CRC value of 49805 (C28D hex) shall be encoded as 00049805". A hex field looks plausible in a hex dump and is silently unverifiable by every conformant reader. Pinned by the_field_is_decimal_not_hexadecimal, which asserts both the positive and assert_ne! against the hex form.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, all four met:
- reference vector + named catalog variant -> the_kermit_catalog_check_value_matches
- write/reopen round-trip verifies -> a_written_file_carries_a_crc_that_verifies_on_reopen
- flipped DATA byte: open_verified Err, open warns -> a_flipped_data_byte_is_rejected_by_open_verified_but_tolerated_by_open
- CrcPolicy::Omit writes exactly b"00000000" -> the_omit_policy_writes_the_not_computed_field_rather_than_nothing

DESIGN NOTES BEYOND THE BEAD:
- StoredCrc has four states, not three. Added Missing (data set ends before its CRC field does) alongside Absent/Value/Malformed so pre-CRC files -- every file this workspace wrote before today -- are not slandered as corrupt. Only Value can conflict, so open_verified accepts both legacy and opt-out files. Covered by a_pre_crc_file_still_opens_and_is_not_called_corrupt.
- Crc16 is incremental. The writers hold HEADER/TEXT/DATA as three buffers; concatenating to hash would double peak memory on the ~768 MB spectral files this exists to support. splitting_the_input_does_not_change_the_result checks every split point.
- Table-driven, built in a const fn. Bitwise is ~8 ops/byte; over 768 MB that is >1s on every write and every open. 512 bytes of rodata, no startup cost.
- A3 helper landed as specified: resolve_segment_offsets(&Header, &Metadata) -> SegmentOffsets extracted from store_raw_data_as_dataframe, which now calls it. last_byte() takes a max across TEXT/DATA/ANALYSIS rather than assuming DATA is last, since §3.7 does not promise segment ordering.
- write_segments() collapsed the duplicated three-write tail in write_fcs_file_with and write_inline_fcs into one place, so .fcz inline files get the CRC too.

SCOPE NOT TAKEN: chained datasets. computed_crc() returns a descriptive Err rather than a wrong number -- see flow-crates-x17.8, now blocked on flow-crates-x17.10, a P1 bug filed from this work ($NEXTDATA is treated as file-absolute but §3.3.31 defines it data-set-relative, wrong for 3+ dataset chains).

Two clippy warnings introduced and fixed (doc_lazy_continuation in write_segments docs; unused std::io::Write in compress.rs after the write_all calls moved out). The two remaining flow-fcs warnings, write.rs:337 and :1014, are blame-verified pre-existing (31bd355c, 968561c2) and tracked by flow-crates-hp6.

## Why
flow-autospectral joint unmix and variant search use faer::Mat<f64> (joint.rs, variants.rs). On Apple NEON that is half the SIMD lanes and 2× the DRAM traffic vs f32. R AutoSpectral is typically double, so this is a quality-checked A/B, not a blind cast. Residual and abundance agreement vs the f64 path (and vs-R) must hold before any keep.

Joint 10,000 events × 20 detectors: f64 FMA floor ~1 ms, measured 2.096 ms keep (ratio ~2×, on-roofline for occupancy). The encoding lever is the remaining width tax, largest at 200k×64 (35 ms MATRIX snapshot).

## Strategy
None of the existing PERF_STRATEGIES cards is this (they already kept hoist/scratch/layout). New experiment: f32 faer (or f32 apply + f64 factor) at 200,000 events × 64 detectors.

## Next
Criterion joint_unmix MATRIX size; compare abundances/residuals to f64; keep only if ≥5% and quality holds.

title: fcs: writer silently corrupts TEXT when a value contains the delimiter under FCS 2.0/3.0
description: Surfaced by flow-crates-1xb Task 5, when the forced form-feed delimiter was removed from write.rs tests and the default space delimiter was exercised for the first time. write::conformance_on_write_tests::the_writer_preserves_the_declared_version_rather_than_imposing_one now fails on its FCS2.0 iteration: v3_2_fcs() sets $CYT = "Test Cytometer" (a value containing a space), and with the default space delimiter this desyncs the TEXT segment on reopen (panic: 'No $P1N keyword stored', diagnostic dump shows keys and values swapped, e.g. '262144 = $P2B'). Root cause: fcs/src/text.rs Escaping::for_version() returns Escaping::None for V1_0/V2_0/V3_0 (FCS 2.0/3.0 have no TEXT escape mechanism per spec), and build_text_segment in fcs/src/write.rs only rejects empty values under Escaping::Doubled (3.1+) -- it never validates that a value/key is free of the chosen delimiter under Escaping::None. So for FCS 2.0/3.0, writing any value or keyword that contains the delimiter character silently corrupts the file rather than erroring. Fix should add a write-time check, analogous to the existing empty-value check, that rejects (rather than silently emits) a value or key containing the delimiter when escaping is Escaping::None.
close_reason: Duplicate of flow-crates-2s7, filed earlier the same day from the flow-crates-1xb Task 4 review. Same defect (no delimiter-in-value guard under Escaping::None for FCS 1.0/2.0/3.0) and same proposed fix. The concrete reproducer and diagnostic dump from this issue have been folded into flow-crates-2s7's notes rather than discarded.

title: Writer silently corrupts pre-3.1 FCS when a keyword value contains the delimiter
description:
Under Escaping::None (FCS 1.0/2.0/3.0), fcs/src/text.rs escape_into writes a delimiter-bearing keyword value raw. The resulting TEXT segment reads back desynchronized - every field after the offending value shifts - with no error at write time and no error at read time. This is the same corruption class that flow-crates-1xb fixed for FCS 3.1+, but pre-3.1 versions have no escape mechanism, so there is no valid encoding for that input at all.

Because there is no legal encoding, the writer should REJECT the value rather than emit a corrupt file. The plumbing to detect it landed with flow-crates-1xb: the 'escaping' value is already in scope in serialize_metadata (fcs/src/write.rs, next to the empty-value guard), so the check is a few lines.

Found by the Task 4 reviewer on branch fcs-column-decode-and-delimiter-escaping. Pre-existing; outside that task's brief, so deliberately not fixed there.
acceptance_criteria: Writing a keyword value that contains the active delimiter under V1_0/V2_0/V3_0 returns an Err naming the keyword, instead of producing a file that reads back with shifted fields. Test covers at least one pre-3.1 version.
notes:
Related: flow-crates-1xb (the 3.1+ half of this), flow-crates-aht (same corruption class, tru-ols export).

REPRODUCER (found independently during flow-crates-1xb Task 5, when the forced form-feed delimiter came out of the write.rs tests and the default space delimiter was exercised for the first time):
write::conformance_on_write_tests::the_writer_preserves_the_declared_version_rather_than_imposing_one fails on its V2_0 iteration. The v3_2_fcs() helper sets $CYT = 'Test Cytometer'; with the default space delimiter the TEXT segment desyncs on reopen. The diagnostic dump shows every field after $CYT shifted by one, keys and values swapped:
  $CYT = Test
  262144 = $P2B
  32 = $P2N
  Cytometer = $P1B
  FL1-A = $P2R
  FSC-A = $P1R
Panic is 'No $P1N keyword stored'. Fix should add a write-time guard beside the existing empty-value guard in serialize_metadata (fcs/src/write.rs) that rejects a key or value containing the delimiter when escaping is Escaping::None. flow-crates-92q was filed for this same defect and closed as a duplicate.

title: fcs: absolutize() tiebreak fails on large multi-data-set files
description:
absolutize() in fcs/src/file.rs disambiguates data-set-relative from file-absolute offsets by preferring relative unless the relative reading runs past EOF. That EOF check is the only tiebreak, and it degrades as files get larger.

Failure case: three 10 MB data sets in a 30 MB file. Data set 2 starts at byte 10,000,000 and its HEADER declares TEXT begin as 10,000,058 (file-absolute, which real vendors do emit -- our own two-data-set .lmd-style fixture writes offsets this way). The relative reading gives 20,000,058, still well inside a 30 MB file, so the EOF guard does not fire and we silently resolve TEXT into the middle of data set 3.

The guard's reliability is inversely proportional to file size, which is backwards: multi-data-set files are the large ones.

Proposed fix: replace the magnitude heuristic with a structural one. Resolve TEXT under the relative reading, verify the byte at text_start is a legal delimiter per s3.2.6 (ASCII 1-126, and in practice non-alphanumeric) and that the segment parses into keyword/value pairs with the required keys present; fall back to the absolute reading if it does not. Structure disambiguates where magnitude cannot. Keep the tracing::warn! on whichever path is taken as non-conformant.

Needs a fixture with a chained data set far enough into a large file that both readings land in bounds -- the existing tests are all small enough that the EOF guard masks the problem.
notes: Surfaced while discussing FCS s2.2.1/2.2.2/2.2.3 terminology. See bd memory fcs-offsets-are-dataset-relative and fcs-spec-file-vs-dataset-wording. Follow-up to flow-crates-x17.10.

title: fcs: OTHER offset scan was bounded by TEXT, but DATA may precede TEXT
description:
Header::get_other_offsets bounded the OTHER offset-pair scan at text_offset.start(). FCS 3.2 s3.1 Example 3 (FCS3.2******202451**203140****1792**202450*******0*******0) is a legal HEADER whose DATA segment precedes TEXT, so on such a file the scan ran across the entire DATA segment -- 200,659 bytes in the spec's own example -- treating any 16 bytes of event data that happen to be ASCII digits as an OTHER segment offset pair.

Fixed by Header::header_end(), which takes the minimum declared start among TEXT/DATA/ANALYSIS that is >= 58. FCS 3.1 Table 1 spelled the bound as 'beginning of next segment'; FCS 3.2 Table 2 drops that wording but the structure is unchanged. Zero starts are skipped -- they mean the segment is absent or lives past the 99,999,999-byte limit and is declared only in TEXT -- and TEXT is always a usable fallback since s3.2.3 requires it within that limit.

Note the off-by-one: the filter must be >= 58, not > 58. A segment beginning at exactly byte 58 is the tightest legal bound (HEADER with no OTHER pairs) and was initially discarded.

Tests in fcs/src/header.rs::other_segment_bounds_tests. The DATA-before-TEXT fixture opens its DATA segment with the ASCII bytes '     100     200' so the failure is deterministic rather than dependent on float bit patterns; without the fix it reports other_offsets == [100..=200].
notes: Found by the user quoting FCS 3.1 s3.1.1 verbatim, including Example 3 and Table 1's 'beginning of next segment' bound for the OTHER field. Follow-up to flow-crates-x17.11.
close_reason: Fixed in fcs/src/header.rs: Header::header_end() bounds the OTHER scan at the minimum declared segment start >= 58, not at TEXT. Three tests added in other_segment_bounds_tests covering the normal case, the DATA-before-TEXT case (spec Example 3), and the zeroed-offset case. Discrimination verified: reverting header_end to [*text.start()] makes the Example 3 test report other_offsets == [100..=200] read out of the DATA segment. 151 flow-fcs tests pass (was 148), workspace check clean, clippy unchanged at 52.

title: fcs: CRC range ignores OTHER segments, so a file whose final segment is OTHER fails verification
description:
FCS 3.2 §3.7 defines the CRC range as ending "with the last byte of the final segment of the data set (which may be a TEXT, DATA, ANALYSIS or OTHER segment)". §3.6 and the HEADER table (spec p.6, bytes 58-65 / 66-73 and onward) put OTHER segment offsets in the HEADER, in 8-byte start/end pairs after the fixed 58 bytes, in any number.

Header (fcs/src/header.rs:18) has only text_offset/data_offset/analysis_offset and Header::from_mmap reads only the fixed 58 bytes -- the OTHER pairs are silently ignored, without error. SegmentOffsets::last_byte() (fcs/src/file.rs:168) therefore maxes over three segments where the spec names four.

FAILURE MODE: a vendor file whose final segment is an OTHER segment placed after DATA. computed_crc() hashes a range that stops short of the real end, so the stored CRC never matches. Fcs::open logs a spurious corruption warning, and Fcs::open_verified REJECTS A VALID FILE. That is worse than the pre-CRC behaviour, because it turns an unreadable-but-harmless gap into a false accusation.

REACHABILITY IS NARROW BUT REAL. §3.6 requires all OTHER segments to sit within the first 99,999,999 bytes of the data set, because the HEADER offset fields are 8 ASCII digits. So on a large file DATA is necessarily last and OTHER cannot be. The exposure is small files that write an OTHER segment after DATA.

Found while walking the §3.7 CRC steps after flow-crates-x17.3 landed.
design:
Two pieces. (1) Header gains other_offsets: Vec<RangeInclusive<usize>>, parsed from byte 58 onward in 16-byte pairs until the TEXT segment start is reached (that is the only available terminator -- the HEADER has no count field). Guard against a malformed pair claiming a range past EOF. (2) SegmentOffsets grows an `other` field and last_byte() folds it into the max.

Note the parse terminator is a judgement call: HEADER length is implicitly text_offset.start(). A file with no OTHER segments has nothing between byte 58 and TEXT, so the loop runs zero times and behaviour is unchanged -- which is the common case and must stay free.

Interaction with flow-crates-x17.10: once data-set-relative offsets are fixed, OTHER offsets are relative to the data set start too.
acceptance_criteria: A synthetic file with an OTHER segment written after DATA round-trips: write, reopen, verify_crc() passes and open_verified succeeds. A file with zero OTHER segments parses to an empty other list and its CRC range is byte-identical to today. Header::from_mmap does not error on a file with OTHER offsets it cannot make sense of -- it ignores them, consistent with the crate reader-tolerance stance.
close_reason:
Implemented: OTHER segments now parsed from the HEADER and folded into the CRC range.

fcs/src/header.rs
- HEADER_SIZE = 58 promoted to a pub const (write.rs now re-exports it instead of
  defining its own copy).
- Header gained other_offsets: Vec<RangeInclusive<usize>>, parsed by the new
  get_other_offsets(). Per S3.6 the HEADER is not fixed-length: any number of extra
  8-byte start/end pairs may follow byte 58, with no count field, so the only
  terminator is text_offset.start(). Parsing is deliberately lenient (filter_map, not
  ?) because S2.2.11 pads unused HEADER space with ASCII spaces -- a blank pair is
  padding, not corruption. Files with no OTHER segments allocate nothing.
- New Header::from_bytes(&[u8]); from_mmap is now the base==0 case delegating to it.
  All get_* helpers widened from &Mmap to &[u8] (deref coercion keeps callers source-
  compatible).

fcs/src/file.rs
- SegmentOffsets gained pub other; last_byte() now maxes OTHER ends in alongside
  TEXT/DATA/ANALYSIS, which is what S3.7 actually requires ('TEXT, DATA, ANALYSIS or
  OTHER' -- four candidates, we only considered three).
- resolve_segment_offsets rebases each OTHER range through absolutize() like every
  other offset.

Test: write.rs::the_crc_range_includes_a_trailing_other_segment. Hand-assembles a
74-byte HEADER (58 + one OTHER pair), TEXT, DATA, a trailing OTHER blob, then a
correct CRC. Asserts segments.other, last_byte(), computed_crc(), stored_crc(), and
that the events still read back.

Discrimination verified: forcing other_end = 0 in last_byte() makes the test fail
with 'a valid file with a trailing OTHER segment must not be refused: CRC mismatch
... file stores 42 but its bytes hash to 30283'. The fixture blob deliberately opens
with eight ASCII digits ('00000042 vendor...') so the bug surfaces as a false
corruption rejection rather than as a silently-skipped check -- a vendor blob
starting with an ID or timestamp is ordinary, and the rejection is the harsher of
the two failure modes.

Verification: 148 flow-fcs tests pass (was 147), cargo check --workspace
--all-targets: 0 errors, clippy -p flow-fcs: 52 warnings, unchanged from HEAD.

title: fcs: parse_spillover overflows on attacker-controlled $SPILLOVER dimension
description: fcs/src/keyword/helpers.rs:145 computes expected_matrix_size = n_parameters * n_parameters and matrix_start = 1 + n_parameters with unchecked arithmetic, where n_parameters is parsed directly from the \$SPILLOVER value in an untrusted file's TEXT segment. A value near usize::MAX panics in debug builds and wraps in release, after which the slice bounds check at parts[matrix_start..matrix_start + expected_matrix_size] is the only thing standing between us and a bad index. This is reached on every Fcs::open of a file carrying \$SPILLOVER, \$SPILL or \$COMP, so the blast radius is every file read, not just unmixed products. Found while adding parse_mixing_matrix (flow-crates-x17.5), whose equivalent arithmetic is now checked and covered by keyword::tests::mixing_matrix::an_absurd_declared_size_does_not_overflow.
acceptance_criteria: parse_spillover("18446744073709551615,x") returns None rather than panicking, under a debug build; a test mirroring an_absurd_declared_size_does_not_overflow covers it.

title: tru-ols: stamp unmixed products as FCS3.2
description: Unmixed products get emitted as FCS3.2; raw passthrough writes keep their source version (no change to peacoqc-cli or the fcz round-trip -- 3.2 must NOT become the global writer default). In the unmixed builder: set header.version = Version::V3_2; derive $BEGINDATETIME/$ENDDATETIME (ISO 8601) from the source $DATE/$BTIM/$ETIM while keeping the originals for 3.1 readers; migrate $PLATEID/$PLATENAME/$WELLID to $CARRIERID/$CARRIERTYPE/$LOCATIONID keeping the originals; set $ORIGINALITY='DataModified' and $LAST_MODIFIER='tru-ols <version>'. $CYT is required in 3.2 and is inherited from the stained source -- verify it survives the keyword strip at fcs_integration.rs:232.
acceptance_criteria: Round-trip test at fcs_integration.rs:1400 asserts version FCS3.2, $CYT present, $ORIGINALITY='DataModified'; a peacoqc-cli passthrough write still emits its source version.
close_reason: Unmixed builder now stamps FCS3.2 via new fcs::upgrade module: header.version=V3_2 plus keyword migration ($DATE+$BTIM/$ETIM -> $BEGINDATETIME/$ENDDATETIME through new fcs::datetime::iso8601_from_fcs_date_and_time; $PLATEID/$PLATENAME/$WELLID -> $CARRIERID/$CARRIERTYPE/$LOCATIONID). Deprecated originals kept for 3.1 readers; migration is idempotent and never overwrites an instrument-written target. $ORIGINALITY/$LAST_MODIFIER/$LAST_MODIFIED already written by provenance. Round-trip test asserts version, $CYT, $ORIGINALITY, $BEGINDATETIME, $LOCATIONID, $CARRIERTYPE; new write.rs test pins that passthrough writes preserve their source version across V2_0/V3_0/V3_1/V3_2. Version now derives PartialEq+Eq (it already derived Hash).

title: fcs: MixedKeyword::MixingMatrix rectangular matrix keyword
description: $SPILLOVER's encoding assumes a square n x n matrix -- parse_spillover (fcs/src/keyword/helpers.rs:128) hardcodes expected_matrix_size = n_parameters * n_parameters. The TRU-OLS mixing matrix is rectangular (detectors x endmembers), so it needs its own variant. Encoding, in the same CSV style as $SPILLOVER: $TRUOLS_MIXMAT/<nDet>,<nEm>,<det1>..<detN>,<em1>..<emM>,<v11>..<vNM>. Touch points: variant + StringableKeyword::get_str arm in fcs/src/keyword/mod.rs:48; serializer arm in the MixedKeyword match at write.rs:598 mirroring SPILLOVER; parse_mixing_matrix in helpers.rs reusing parse_float_with_comma_decimal; dispatch arm in parsing.rs:101.
acceptance_criteria: A rectangular matrix survives serialize -> parse round-trip with names and both dimensions intact; malformed input (wrong value count) returns None rather than panicking.
close_reason: Added MixedKeyword::MixingMatrix (n_detectors, n_endmembers, detector_names, endmember_names, row-major matrix_values) with get_str + Hash arms; parse_mixing_matrix in helpers.rs with fully checked arithmetic; $TRUOLS_MIXMAT dispatch arm in parsing.rs; serializer arm in write.rs. 5 new tests: rectangular parse, name-split boundary, malformed fall-through (6 cases), usize::MAX overflow, and a write->reopen round trip verified to fail when the serializer's dimension order is flipped. The oversized-keyword layout test now uses the real keyword (17 KB at 64x40) instead of a stand-in string.

title: fcs: 3.2 keywords and per-version conformance rules
description: Add StringKeyword::{UNSTAINEDINFO, UNSTAINEDCENTERS} plus dispatch arms in fcs/src/keyword/parsing.rs alongside the existing FLOWRATE/CARRIERID arms -- these are the spec-native home for unstained-control description and feed the provenance work. Then extend the validator that already exists: Metadata::validate_text_segment_keywords(&Header) (fcs/src/metadata.rs:201) walks header.version.get_required_keywords() and bails on the first missing key; change it to accumulate Vec<String>. Put new per-version rules in a NEW fcs/src/conformance.rs module, one function per rule keyed by Version, so the follow-up VersionSpec refactor is a mechanical move. 3.2 rules: $CYT required; $PnB divisible by 8; $MODE must be 'L' if present; $TIMESTEP required when a $PnN is TIME; $BYTEORD restricted to 1,2,3,4 / 4,3,2,1; deprecated keywords warned not rejected. Called from write_fcs_file as a warning by default, error under a strict flag.
acceptance_criteria: UNSTAINEDINFO/UNSTAINEDCENTERS parse and round-trip; validate accumulates all violations rather than the first; write_fcs_file warns (not errors) on a non-conformant 3.2 file by default.
close_reason: Added StringKeyword::{UNSTAINEDINFO,UNSTAINEDCENTERS} + parsing dispatch + round-trip tests; validate_text_segment_keywords now delegates to Metadata::missing_required_keywords and reports every miss; new fcs/src/conformance.rs with six per-version rules (required keywords, $BYTEORD value, $MODE=L, $PnB byte alignment, $TIMESTEP for TIME parameter, deprecated keywords) keyed by Version; WriteOptions{ConformancePolicy::{Warn,Strict}} wired into write_fcs_file_with. 15 conformance tests, 106 total green.

title: fcs: size-aware estimate_text_segment_size for large keywords
description: estimate_text_segment_size (fcs/src/write.rs:441) assumes a flat 50 bytes per keyword (keywords.len() * 50). The $TRUOLS_MIXMAT keyword for a 64-detector x 40-endmember panel is ~30 KB of ASCII, which blows the estimate badly enough to risk exhausting the 8-iteration offset-convergence budget in write_fcs_file (write.rs:91). Make the estimator ask each keyword for its serialized length instead of assuming a constant.
acceptance_criteria: Estimator reflects actual serialized keyword length; a metadata set containing one 30 KB keyword converges within the existing iteration budget, covered by a test.
notes:
Implemented by DELETING estimate_text_segment_size rather than making it size-aware.

Rationale: the estimator existed only to seed the offset-convergence loop. Seeding
from an actual serialize_metadata pass (data_start/data_end = 0) costs one extra
serialization but has zero estimation error, so keyword size stops mattering
entirely - a strictly better outcome than a smarter estimate.

Replaced with a shared helper in fcs/src/write.rs:
  - HEADER_SIZE, MAX_LAYOUT_PASSES consts
  - struct FcsLayout { text_segment, text_start, text_end, data_start, data_end }
  - fn resolve_layout(metadata, text_start, n_events, n_params, data_len)

resolve_layout takes text_start explicitly so $NEXTDATA-chained datasets (which
do not start at byte 58) can use it. Rewired write_fcs_file, compress.rs
write_inline_fcs, and three duplicated convergence loops in tests onto it.

Acceptance criterion met via test a_very_large_keyword_still_resolves_to_a_stable_layout:
26 KB single keyword (64x40 signed floats, the shape $TRUOLS_MIXMAT will emit),
asserts the resolved layout is a genuine fixpoint (re-serializing with the
reported offsets reproduces TEXT byte-for-byte), not merely that it did not error.

Note: the plan's '~30 KB' figure for a 64x40 matrix is high - actual is ~26 KB at
six decimal places with signs. Test asserts >20 KB rather than padding the fixture
to match the estimate.

Convergence is structural: $BEGINDATA/$ENDDATA only change TEXT length when their
digit count changes, so it settles in <=2 passes at any keyword size.
close_reason: Implemented and tested; see issue notes.

title: fcs: decide fast-flow multi-dataset UX (cycle / merge / keep-separate)
description:
Follow-up from flow-crates-1mg ($NEXTDATA / open_all() traversal).

open_all() returns Vec<Fcs>, order/length already encoding dataset index/count — deliberately UX-agnostic. Need an app-layer decision on how fast-flow surfaces multi-dataset files (e.g. Beckman .lmd) to users:
- Cycle/browse: index into the Vec, one active dataset at a time (mirrors flowCore's read.FCS(dataset=i))
- Merge: pass Vec<Fcs> into existing concatenate_events() in fcs/src/write.rs, treat as one unified run
- Keep all loaded separately: each dataset becomes its own loaded file/tab (mirrors FlowIO's read_multiple_data_sets())

Neither flowCore nor FlowIO auto-merge by default — both leave that as an explicit follow-on step. Could support more than one of these depending on user intent (deferred call, not to be baked into the crate API).

title: fcs: no $NEXTDATA traversal — multi-dataset FCS files (incl. Beckman .lmd) unreadable
description:
Reported upstream: https://github.com/jrmoynihan/flow/issues/21 (item 3)

open() parses exactly one data segment. $NEXTDATA is listed in version.rs's required-keyword sets and written by write.rs (always as "0"), but nothing reads it back to seek to and parse a chained second data set.

Multi-dataset FCS files are legal per spec, and Beckman .lmd files are specifically two chained data sets under the hood — so .lmd is entirely unreadable today. Reporter notes FlowIO (Python) implements this in ~40 lines (utils.py) as a reference.

This is a feature gap, not a memory-safety bug: single-dataset files are unaffected.
acceptance_criteria: open() (or a new open_all()/multi-dataset API) follows $NEXTDATA to parse subsequent data segments in the same file, returning a Vec of parsed datasets (or similar) instead of assuming exactly one. At least one multi-dataset fixture file (synthetic or real .lmd) parses all segments correctly. Existing single-dataset callers unaffected (NEXTDATA=0 short-circuits to today's behavior).
close_reason:
Implemented $NEXTDATA traversal via a new Fcs::open_all(path) -> Result<Vec<Fcs>>, alongside the unchanged Fcs::open() (still returns only dataset 1, same cost as before for the ~100% common single-dataset case).

Design: factored open()'s body into a private parse_one_dataset(file_access: AccessWrapper, header: Header) -> Result<(Self, usize)>, which now also reads back $NEXTDATA's value (0 if absent) after building the Fcs. open() calls it once and discards the offset; open_all() loops while next_offset != 0, with a HashSet-based cycle guard against a corrupt file whose chain loops back on an already-visited TEXT offset.

Key discovery before writing any code: $NEXTDATA has no dedicated IntegerKeyword variant — parse_fixed_keywords (keyword/parsing.rs) has no match arm for "NEXTDATA", so it always falls through to StringKeyword::Other. parse_one_dataset reads it via metadata.get_string_keyword("$NEXTDATA") + get_str().trim().parse::<usize>(), not get_integer_keyword (which would never find it).

The harder problem: only dataset 1 has the fixed 58-byte primary HEADER; dataset 2+ has no repeated HEADER, only a new TEXT segment (pointed to by $NEXTDATA, confirmed as an absolute file offset per version.rs's keyword docs) followed by its own DATA segment. There's no explicit "TEXT end" for these datasets — it can only be derived as ($BEGINDATA - 1), and $BEGINDATA is itself a keyword/value pair inside the TEXT segment being bounded. Solved with two small helpers:
- find_begindata_offset(mmap, text_start): a bounded, early-stopping delimiter tokenizer (mirrors Metadata::from_mmap's keyword/value alternation exactly) that stops the instant it finds $BEGINDATA, so it never risks reading into DATA bytes (which could coincidentally contain the delimiter byte value).
- header_for_dataset_at(mmap, text_start, version): packages that into a synthetic Header { text_offset: text_start..=(begin_data-1), data_offset: 0..=0, ... } — data_offset is 0..=0 deliberately, because store_raw_data_as_dataframe already has an existing fallback (checks metadata's $BEGINDATA/$ENDDATA when header.data_offset is 0) that this reuses for free, so dataset 2+ needed no changes to the DATA-parsing path at all.

Test (write.rs, TDD red->green): hand-built a synthetic two-dataset file — dataset 1 with a real primary HEADER whose $NEXTDATA points at dataset 2's TEXT start, dataset 2 appended directly as TEXT+DATA with no second HEADER. Converged dataset 1's TEXT/DATA layout AND its $NEXTDATA value together in one loop (changing $NEXTDATA's digit count shifts dataset 1's TEXT length, which shifts where dataset 2 starts). Asserted open() still returns only dataset 1's values, and open_all() returns both datasets' distinct values in order. Confirmed this failed to compile before implementation (Fcs::open_all didn't exist).

Verification: cargo test -p flow-fcs --lib: 78/78 passed (77 pre-existing + 1 new). cargo clippy -p flow-fcs --lib --tests: 0 errors, 0 new warnings (33 pre-existing warnings elsewhere in the crate, none touching the new code).

Design rationale for keeping open()/open_all() separate rather than merging: eager-cost avoidance (a caller wanting only dataset 1 doesn't pay to parse+DataFrame-build datasets 2..N), failure isolation (a bad dataset 2 doesn't invalidate a good dataset 1), and call-site ergonomics (no .first() boilerplate needed at every existing single-dataset call site). Matches what flowCore and FlowIO independently converged on.

Follow-up: flow-crates-vjd (multi-dataset UX decision at the app layer — cycle/merge/keep-separate) is now unblocked.

title: fcs: record stride miscomputed for non-byte-aligned $PnB (bit-packed) files
description:
Reported upstream: https://github.com/jrmoynihan/flow/issues/21 (item 2)

metadata.rs:~324-344 computes record stride by rounding each parameter's $PnB up to a byte boundary independently, then summing: bytes = (bits_value + 7) / 8; total_bytes += bytes. Same root cause in datatype.rs::get_bytes_for_bits.

This is only correct when every parameter is individually byte-aligned. A legal FCS 3.1 file with $PnB/10/ on 8 channels has an 80-bit (10-byte) packed record; per-parameter rounding computes 8 x 2 = 16 bytes instead, misreading the entire data segment.

Deprecated in FCS 3.2 (change #13) so should be rare in modern exports, but real in older archived files. Currently causes a silent mis-parse rather than a clean rejection.
acceptance_criteria: Stride computed as ceil(sum of all $PnB bits / 8), not sum of per-parameter ceil(bits/8). If per-parameter bit-packing within a shared byte is out of scope for this fix, at minimum detect the non-byte-aligned case and return a clear error instead of silently misreading the file.
close_reason: Fixed record stride math: calculate_bytes_per_event() now sums raw $PnB bit widths across all parameters and rounds up once (ceil(sum(bits)/8)), instead of rounding each parameter individually before summing. The old approach overcounted for bit-packed (non-byte-aligned $PnB) records, e.g. 8x $PnB=10 params: correct=ceil(80/8)=10 bytes, old buggy=8*ceil(10/8)=16 bytes. Added a dedicated bit-packed read path (parse_bit_packed_data + a hand-rolled MSB-first BitReader in file.rs) used only when at least one parameter's $PnB isn't a multiple of 8; the existing byte-aligned fast/variable-width paths are untouched for the common case. New test bit_packed_pnb10_record_uses_correct_stride_and_decodes hand-packs 8x10-bit channels and round-trips through calculate_bytes_per_event + Fcs::open. Verified true red state via git-stash-isolated pre-fix code (test failed with predicted 16 vs 10). Also fixed a pre-existing clippy manual_div_ceil lint on the unrelated (dead-code, zero call sites) get_bytes_for_bits. cargo test -p flow-fcs --lib: 77/77 pass. cargo clippy -p flow-fcs --lib --tests: 0 errors, no new warnings. Known limitation (documented in code): bit order is spec-derived (MSB-first) and internally consistent but not validated against a real vendor's on-disk bit order, since FCS 3.2 deprecated bit-packing specifically because vendors disagreed on this.

title: PARALLEL_BYTE_THRESHOLD: the upward direction (1 MiB vs 4 MiB) is unmeasured
description:
Task 12 of the flow-crates-3si plan probed the threshold DOWNWARD and positively ruled out 256 KiB: fcs2_int16_50000ev_8par_random.fcs has 781.25 KiB of DATA, and forcing the parallel branch on it regressed decode by +31.49% [+23.30, +40.84] and +43.78% [+37.21, +50.72] across two independent cycles, both p=0.00, criterion verdict 'Performance has regressed' both times. So the constant stays at 1 << 20.

What remains unprobed is the UPWARD direction. Nothing in the current bench suite distinguishes 1 MiB from 4 MiB, because no corpus fixture lands between them: the largest corpus DATA segment is 781.25 KiB (below both) and the synthetic fixture is 76.3 MiB (above both). All candidates therefore select the same branch on every committed fixture, so the Task 12 sweep over 256 KiB / 1 MiB / 4 MiB executed identical machine code for the 1 MiB and 4 MiB rows -- it measured nothing about that boundary.

To close it, one of:
  (a) generate a ~2 MiB fixture (e.g. ~65k events x 8 params x 4 bytes) and run the probe the same way Task 12 did, or
  (b) extend the synthetic generator in fcs/benches/lazy_column_access.rs to take a size parameter and sweep it across the 1-8 MiB band.

Method note, learned the hard way in Task 12: this machine drifts several percent over a long benchmarking session, enough to make an untouched control read 'Performance has regressed' at p=0.00. Carry a control benchmark and interleave the two binaries rather than batching all-before-then-all-after.

Low priority: the cost of being wrong here is a rayon fan-out on files in the 1-4 MiB band that may not pay for itself, which is a few hundred microseconds, not a correctness issue.

title: extract_columns: chunks_exact(bytes_per_event) panics if bytes_per_event is 0
description:
Pre-existing, NOT introduced by the flow-crates-3si column-decode rewrite: both the old decode_row loop (commit 2c8f09f, columns.rs:163-172) and the new fill_events (f0ef529) call chunks_exact/par_chunks_exact on layout.bytes_per_event without guarding against zero. slice::chunks_exact panics when chunk_size == 0, regardless of slice length.

bytes_per_event is the running sum of bytes_per_parameter, so it is 0 exactly when $PAR is 0. Metadata::get_number_of_parameters just reads $PAR as a usize and does not reject 0.

Reachability is UNCONFIRMED — an $PAR 0 file may be rejected earlier in Fcs::open, and Fcs::columns may early-return before reaching extract_columns when there are no parameters to request. Confirm reachability first; if reachable, the fix is a guard in ColumnLayout::from_metadata (reject $PAR 0 as malformed metadata) rather than in the decode loop, so the check is paid once per file instead of once per call.

Found during the Task 9 review of the flow-crates-3si rewrite while verifying that plan.offset + plan.width <= bytes_per_event holds for every layout from_metadata can build (it does — param_offsets is a prefix sum of bytes_per_parameter, so offset+width == sum[0..=i] <= bytes_per_event). The zero case is the one gap in that argument.
notes: Related divergence found in the Task 10 review, same root cause, worth fixing in the same change: the sequential and parallel branches of extract_columns_inner behave DIFFERENTLY when bytes_per_event == 0. The sequential branch calls chunks_exact(0) and panics. The parallel branch's chunk walk computes take = EVENTS_PER_CHUNK.min(rest_bytes.len() / bytes_per_event), which divides by zero -- an arithmetic panic on a different line with a different message. So the same malformed file produces two different panics depending only on DATA size relative to PARALLEL_BYTE_THRESHOLD. A single guard in ColumnLayout::from_metadata (reject $PAR 0) fixes both, which is another argument for siting it there rather than in the decode loop.

title: fcs: non-UTF-8 TEXT keyword values are silently degraded to empty or dropped entirely
description:
Metadata::from_text_segment decodes each TEXT field with str::from_utf8(..).unwrap_or_default(). Real FCS exports routinely carry Latin-1 bytes in free-text keywords ($PnS "µL", $COM "37 °C"), and those bytes are not valid UTF-8, so the whole value collapses to the empty string. Two distinct wrong outcomes follow, depending on where the field sits:

1. Interior field: the keyword is recorded with an empty value. The caller cannot distinguish "the writer emitted an empty value" from "we could not decode it".
2. Unterminated trailing field: the keyword is dropped entirely, no insert, no warning.

Both are silent data loss. Predates the Task-2 tokenizer extraction (flow-crates-1xb) — the extraction deliberately preserved both behaviours so that change could stay a provable no-op, and pinned them with tests in mod from_text_segment_tests (fcs/src/metadata.rs). Discovered by the Task 2 code review.

Options worth weighing: decode lossily (String::from_utf8_lossy) so the keyword survives with replacement characters; decode as Latin-1, which is what the emitting software most likely meant; or surface a decode error. Whichever is chosen, the two paths above should stop disagreeing with each other.

Fixing this means changing the from_text_segment_tests assertions, which currently document the current behaviour rather than endorse it.
acceptance_criteria: A TEXT keyword value containing a non-UTF-8 byte round-trips to something distinguishable from an empty value, and the interior-field and trailing-field paths agree with each other.

title: fcs: Fcs::new() always returns Err (AccessWrapper::new(""))
description:
Fcs::new() (fcs/src/file.rs:400) constructs its file_access as AccessWrapper::new("")?, which is File::open("") -- that returns ENOENT on every platform, so Fcs::new() can never return Ok. Verified empirically 2026-08-08.

It has zero callers in the workspace (rg 'Fcs::new()' across all crates finds none), so nothing is broken today, but it is pub API: any downstream caller reaching for the obvious constructor gets an unconditional error with a confusing message ('No such file or directory').

Found while planning flow-crates-3si -- the bench fixture generator in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-08-fcs-column-decode-and-delimiter-escaping.md originally used it and had to be rerouted through Fcs::open() on a corpus file instead.

Options: (a) delete it as dead API, since for_testing covers the test case and open()/open_all() cover the real one; (b) make file_access an Option; (c) give AccessWrapper a lazy/empty variant. (a) is probably right -- an Fcs with no backing file has no valid mmap, which is exactly what the type says it always has.

title: tru-ols: retire ensure_delimiter_survives_provenance once flow-crates-1xb lands
description:
flow-crates-1xb fixes flow-fcs's writer so it doubles the TEXT delimiter inside keyword values (FCS 3.1+). Once that lands, tru-ols's defensive machinery for the same problem becomes dead weight:

- tru-ols/src/provenance.rs: SAFE_TEXT_DELIMITER (form feed), ensure_delimiter_survives_provenance(fcs), called from both Provenance::write_to and stamp_onto. It rewrites the file's delimiter away from space/NUL before provenance keywords are written.

title: fcs: events_from_inline_fcs bypasses resolve_segment_offsets, reads header.data_offset directly
description:
Final review of the main-reconciliation merge for flow-crates-dzw found that fcs/src/compress.rs:215-216 (events_from_inline_fcs) reads *header.data_offset.start()/.end() directly rather than going through resolve_segment_offsets(header, metadata, dataset_start, file_len) — the same dataset-relative-offset bug class that f0b2922 fixed for the eager path and this merge fixed for the lazy column()/columns()/events() path (see fcs/src/file.rs's data_bytes()).

This is main's own pre-existing code (byte-unchanged by the merge, confirmed identical to main HEAD), and it currently only ever sees single-dataset FCZ1 inline files, so dataset_start is always 0 there today and the bug is latent, not live. But it's the one remaining place in the crate using the old file-absolute-only offset logic instead of the shared resolve_segment_offsets mechanism, so the 'one mechanism' invariant established by f0b2922/this merge isn't quite complete.

Fix: route events_from_inline_fcs's offset resolution through resolve_segment_offsets too, passing dataset_start=0 explicitly (or wiring in a real dataset_start if FCZ1 inline files can ever be non-first in a chain — confirm this can't happen before assuming 0 is always correct).

title: fcs: the blas feature no longer compiles - faer Mat lost into_ndarray
description:
cargo test --workspace --all-features fails to compile flow-fcs:

  error[E0599]: no method named `into_ndarray` found for struct
  `faer::mat::generic::Mat<faer::mat::Ref<f32>>`
    --> fcs/src/matrix.rs:20:36

The call sits inside #[cfg(feature = "blas")] in fcs/src/matrix.rs, alongside `use faer_ext::IntoNdarray;` and `ndarray_linalg::Inverse`. The faer_ext IntoNdarray trait no longer applies to the receiver type after a faer version bump, so the whole blas code path is dead.

CONSEQUENCE: --all-features is not a usable gate for this workspace. Anyone running it -- CI, a release check, or an agent verifying its own work -- gets a compile error unrelated to what they changed, which trains people to ignore it. That is the real cost; the blas path itself is optional and unused by default.

Verified pre-existing on 2026-08-07: fcs/src/matrix.rs is byte-identical to HEAD (1f9508f) and the same code is present there.
design:
Either repair or remove, but do not leave it half-alive. Repair: faer-ext moved the conversion; check the faer-ext version in Cargo.lock against its docs for the current spelling of Mat -> ArrayView (likely a different trait or a &-receiver). Remove: if nothing in the workspace enables blas and the faer-native inverse is adequate, delete the cfg block, the faer-ext/ndarray-linalg optional deps, and the feature entry -- a feature that has never compiled since the bump has no users to break.

Prefer removal unless someone can name a caller: ndarray-linalg drags in a system LAPACK, which is a heavy dependency to carry for a code path that provably does not build.
acceptance_criteria: cargo check --workspace --all-features succeeds. If the blas feature is kept, a test exercises matrix inversion under it; if removed, no reference to blas, faer-ext, or ndarray-linalg remains in any manifest.

title: fcs: use chrono for datetime calendar arithmetic instead of hand-rolled civil_from_days
description: fcs/src/datetime.rs hand-rolls Hinnant's civil_from_days plus Unix-seconds formatting (~55 lines). chrono 0.4.45 is ALREADY in flow-fcs's normal dependency graph via polars-core/polars-arrow/polars-io/object_store (10 edges, verified 2026-08-06), so using it costs zero marginal compile time or binary size. What chrono replaces: now_iso8601_utc, iso8601_utc_from_unix_seconds, civil_from_days, validate_ymd, and most of parse_fcs_date (NaiveDate::parse_from_str with %d-%b-%Y / %d-%b-%y / %Y-%m-%d tried in order). What it does NOT replace: parse_fcs_time, because FCS 3.0's colon-separated hundredths (14:30:00:25) is not a strftime form, and the degrade-to-whole-seconds tolerance on a garbled fraction is a deliberate vendor accommodation. Only Utc and NaiveDate would be used - never Local, which is the source of chrono's RUSTSEC-2020-0159 localtime_r unsoundness.
design: Scope chrono to calendar arithmetic and the standard date parse; keep the FCS-quirk tolerance layer hand-written. chrono stays an internal implementation detail - the public API returns String, so no semver leakage to downstream crates. Prefer chrono over jiff despite jiff's nicer API purely because chrono is already resolved; jiff would be a genuinely new dependency.
acceptance_criteria: All 16 existing fcs::datetime tests pass unchanged - they are the specification and must not be edited to fit the implementation. Additionally: 31-FEB-2024 must yield None rather than today's fabricated 2024-02-31T.. (latent bug the current validate_ymd allows through, since it range-checks components without checking month length).
close_reason: chrono swap landed. datetime.rs now uses Utc::now()/DateTime::from_timestamp for formatting and NaiveDate::parse_from_str over DATE_FORMATS for parsing; civil_from_days and validate_ymd deleted. parse_fcs_time kept hand-written as designed. All 11 pre-existing tests passed UNEDITED (bead said 16; actual count was 11 - the acceptance intent, that the tests are the spec, was met). Latent bug fixed: 31-FEB-2024 now yields None instead of the fabricated 2024-02-31T00:00:00. Two tests added: an_impossible_date_is_rejected_rather_than_emitted and the_two_digit_year_format_is_tried_before_the_four_digit_one. Cargo.lock delta is exactly one line (+chrono edge under flow-fcs), zero new packages - the zero-marginal-cost claim verified after the fact, not just asserted. Gates: flow-fcs lib 129 passed; flow-tru-ols --features flow-fcs all green; cargo check --workspace --all-targets zero errors; clippy clean on datetime.rs/upgrade.rs. NOT committed (conservative profile).
