title: fcs: VersionSpec trait for per-version write/validate behaviour
description: Version is currently a label, not a behaviour selector: it drives exactly two things -- the 6-byte version string in build_header (fcs/src/write.rs:707) and the required-keyword list in validate_text_segment_keywords (fcs/src/metadata.rs:201). build_header emits byte-identical output for V2_0 and V3_2 apart from those six bytes. That is the root cause of the non-conformance addressed by the parent epic. Target: a VersionSpec trait behind Version::spec() -> &'static dyn VersionSpec, with shared rules as default methods or small composable rule structs so overlapping versions share logic. Children: extract fcs/src/conformance.rs rules into VersionSpec impls; add Version::spec(); migrate build_header and validate_text_segment_keywords to dispatch through it.
design: DECIDED, do not relitigate: (1) NOT typestate. A file's version is only known at runtime, after reading HEADER bytes 0-5. Making Fcs generic over version forces a 6-way monomorphizing match at the parse boundary and leaks the type parameter through tru-ols, peacoqc, gates, and flow-knn, all of which hold a concrete Fcs. Use runtime dispatch for a runtime-known property. Note that Rust enum variants are not types, so 'impl Trait for Version::V3_2' is not expressible regardless. (2) Writers and validators ONLY -- the reader stays version-agnostic. Real files routinely violate their declared version; the $BEGINDATA fallback (fcs/src/file.rs:546) and the StringKeyword::Other(Arc<str>) catch-all exist for that reason and are features. A per-version FcsReadable would turn that tolerance into six near-identical impls plus a new class of 'vendor file will not open' bugs. (3) Sequenced AFTER the conformance epic, not before: two dispatch points exist today, that epic adds roughly five more, and extracting the trait now means guessing its shape from two data points.
acceptance_criteria: build_header and keyword validation dispatch through Version::spec(); no version match arms remain scattered outside the version module; reader behaviour is unchanged and the real-world vendor file corpus still opens.

title: fcs: CRC verification for $NEXTDATA-chained datasets
description:
FCS 3.2 §3.3.31 makes $NEXTDATA an offset from the beginning of a data set, so each chained data set has its own byte range and its own CRC field.

As shipped in flow-crates-x17.3, Fcs::computed_crc() returns a descriptive Err for any dataset past the first rather than StoredCrc::Absent (the original wording here) -- the four-state StoredCrc enum describes what is ON DISK, and silently reporting Absent for a field we simply declined to locate would have conflated "writer opted out" with "we did not try". is_first_dataset() (fcs/src/file.rs:426) re-parses the primary 58-byte HEADER and compares TEXT offsets to make the distinction.

Extend verification to chained datasets: resolve each data set start, run resolve_segment_offsets against it, and parse the CRC field at that data set last byte + 1.
acceptance_criteria: A multi-dataset file has its per-dataset CRCs verified rather than reported Absent.
notes:
RESOLVED as part of flow-crates-x17.10, which introduced Fcs::dataset_start.

computed_crc() no longer refuses chained data sets. It now hashes mmap[dataset_start..=segments.last_byte()], and stored_crc() reads the field at last_byte()+1 where last_byte() is resolved against the data set's own base. Both go through the new Fcs::segment_offsets(), which calls resolve_segment_offsets with dataset_start and the file length.

is_first_dataset() survives as 'dataset_start == 0' but is no longer a precondition for anything - it is now just an accessor.

Covered by write.rs open_all_resolves_nextdata_relative_to_each_dataset_start, which asserts all[2].computed_crc() equals crc::compute over data set 3's own bytes.
close_reason: Implemented: FCS offsets are now data-set-relative throughout, with vendor-tolerant absolute fallback. 147 flow-fcs tests + 47 workspace test binaries green; no new clippy warnings (52 before and after).

title: fcs: stream GPU upload column-by-column across files without materializing the joined frame
description:
Follow-up to flow-crates-dzw (lazy per-column loading).

fcs/src/write.rs:296 concatenates datasets via files.iter().map(|f| (*f.data_frame).clone()) — a full copy of every participating DataFrame before the concat even runs. For a multi-file GPU upload (fast-flow uploads raw channel data and compensates in a WebGPU shader), the joined CPU-side frame is pure overhead: the shader only needs each channel's events laid out contiguously across files.

Once column-level access lands, concatenation for upload can iterate channel-by-channel across the file set, appending each file's column directly into the destination buffer, and never build the joined DataFrame at all. Peak memory drops from sum-of-all-frames to one column's worth.

Scope note: this is about the *upload/serialization* path only. write.rs's on-disk concat_fcs_files still needs a real DataFrame and is out of scope.
design: Depends on the column-extraction primitive from flow-crates-dzw. Requires channel-name reconciliation across files (differing $PnN sets / ordering) and agreement on event-count handling when files differ in $TOT. Should not populate the per-file column cache.
acceptance_criteria: Multi-file channel upload path allocates at most one column at a time rather than cloning every DataFrame; benchmark shows peak memory independent of file count.

title: fcs: write channel data straight from mmap into the Tauri IPC buffer
description:
Follow-up to flow-crates-dzw (lazy per-column loading).

fast-flow's get_raw_channel_data (src-tauri/src/commands/legacy/mod.rs:3250) currently: (1) borrows Vec<&[f32]> of fully-materialized columns from the cached Fcs, then (2) reinterprets each via unsafe from_raw_parts and appends into a Vec<u8> IPC buffer. The buffer layout is already channel-contiguous, which exactly matches per-column storage.

Once flow-crates-dzw lands column-level access over the mmap, the CPU-side f32 column becomes an unnecessary intermediate for this path: the strided byte->f32 conversion could write directly into the preallocated IPC buffer, skipping one full copy per channel per request.

Note the gated case: when gate_id is Some, the command filters by event indices, so the direct-write path only applies to the ungated branch (or needs an index-aware variant.
design: Depends on the column-extraction primitive from flow-crates-dzw. Likely shape: a method that takes a &mut [u8] destination plus channel name and performs the stride-parse writing little-endian f32 directly, avoiding Box<[f32]> allocation entirely. Must not populate the OnceLock column cache (that would defeat the memory saving).
acceptance_criteria: Ungated get_raw_channel_data performs zero intermediate per-channel f32 allocations; benchmark shows reduced allocation and equal-or-better latency vs the materialized path.

title: fcs: investigate LazyFrame/streaming engine to reduce eager-parse memory cost
description:
Motivated by two things from https://github.com/jrmoynihan/flow/issues/21: the reporter's design question about in-memory loading limiting parallel comparison of many large FCS files, and the eager-parsing cost identified while designing open_all() (flow-crates-1mg) — parsing every chained dataset fully into a DataFrame even if a caller only wants the first.

Confirmed via Cargo.toml (not assumption): fcs/Cargo.toml and the workspace root already enable Polars' 'lazy' AND 'streaming' features (default-features=false still respected — no new bloat risk). This is a usage gap: file.rs's store_raw_data_as_dataframe always eagerly builds a fully-materialized DataFrame via DataFrame::new(...), never touching LazyFrame or the streaming engine already compiled in.

Scope as an investigation first, not a committed rewrite: measure whether LazyFrame + streaming actually reduces peak memory for our access pattern (mmap'd raw bytes -> columnar floats is a one-time full materialization, not a query-pushdown scenario where Polars streaming usually wins) before committing to a rewrite.
notes:
Design complete: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-05-lazy-fcs-column-loading-design.md

Investigation outcome: Polars LazyFrame/streaming does NOT apply (no scanner to push into; FCS is hand-parsed from mmap). Laziness must be built at the parse layer. Design instead splits Fcs (raw, file-backed, Arc<[OnceLock<Box<[f32]>>]>) from EventDataFrame (owned, droppable, derived), with a single row-major traversal primitive parameterized by column selection.

Scoped honestly: no memory win for files that go through QC (preprocess_fcs materializes everything immediately). Win is in files opened but never analyzed (~35 of 114 .data_frame sites are shape queries), the 2-channel plotting path, and raw/derived correctness.

Staged A/B/C migration described in the spec. Follow-ups: flow-crates-xii, flow-crates-bif.

title: fcs: $DATATYPE A (ASCII) hard-errors instead of degrading gracefully
description:
Reported upstream: https://github.com/jrmoynihan/flow/issues/21 (item 4)

datatype.rs:30 — FcsDataType::from_keyword_str() returns Err(anyhow!("ASCII-encoded string data type not supported")) for $DATATYPE A. Deprecated in the current FCS standard, but present in some older real-world files.

Current behavior (explicit, loud error) is arguably fine for a deprecated format — low priority. Worth deciding intentionally rather than leaving as an accident of what's implemented: either (a) confirm this is a deliberate won't-fix and close as such, or (b) implement basic ASCII decimal parsing if real user files surface.
acceptance_criteria: Either: explicit decision recorded to not support $DATATYPE A (close as won't-fix / by-design), or ASCII-encoded integer/float parsing implemented and covered by a fixture test.
close_reason: Won't-fix: existing behavior (explicit Err on $DATATYPE=A) is already the correct failure mode. FCS deprecated the ASCII datatype specifically because vendor implementations disagreed on interpretation, and no supported instrument/tool in this ecosystem emits it — rejecting it is a deliberate spec-driven decision, not a gap. Changes made: (1) updated the doc comment on FcsDataType::from_keyword_str (fcs/src/datatype.rs) to state explicitly that ASCII is deprecated by spec and intentionally unsupported, referencing this issue, so it reads as a decision rather than an oversight; (2) added a unit test (from_keyword_str_rejects_deprecated_ascii_datatype) confirming the Err path, since none existed anywhere in the crate previously. Verified: cargo test -p flow-fcs --lib passes 79/79 (was 78 before this test addition); cargo clippy -p flow-fcs --lib --tests shows zero new warnings (only pre-existing, unrelated warnings in the analyze_benchmarks bin).
